newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share trade strong ahead of holidays.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share trade strong ahead of holidays.

text.p: Trading was bullish as the Nigerian stock market wrapped up the week's business on Thursday for the Christian Easter festivities, dealers said.
The all-share index ended at 8561.38 from 8561.40 on Wednesday, buoyed by growing activities in blue chip stocks.

"Blue chips made gains on increasing demand for them, resulting in big price appreciations," said one trader. "The bullish tendencies look set to continue in the coming weeks because investors want shares at any price."
Key bank stocks witnessed active trading as did food companies.
Cadbury soared by 1.00 naira as traders bought a large quantity. It closed at 39.00 naira.
First Bank closed at 19.00 naira, up 25 kobo while Union Bank and UBA gained 20 kobo each to close, respectively at 16.10 naira and 13.80 naira.
Conglomerates soared on better prospects. PZ Industries PZIN.LG closed 45 kobo up at 26.65 naira and Lever Brothers was up 30 kobo at 26.50 naira.
John Holt rose on speculation by five kobo to 9.70 naira and UAC closed 25 kobo more at 15.75 naira.
Traders said oil shares, usually the toast of the market, would receive a better reception next week as a fuel scarcity which grounded them all week eased completely on Thursday.
Unipetrol, the dearest stock on the exchange, added 10 kobo to close at 76.10 naira.
Few stocks fell on Friday. Thomas Wyatt fell to 4.65 naira, down five kobo because there were no buyers for it.
Paint makers suffered slight drops. Chemical and Allied Products, at 4.38 naira and African Paints Paints at 1.36 naira, lost one kobo apiece.
